summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers on install and require
details: The package ships a `postinstall` script running `node beacon.cjs` and an `index.js` that invokes the same beacon on require. Both paths POST the installer's `os.hostname()`, install path (`__dirname`), current working directory, Node.js version, and package name to a hardcoded bare-IP HTTP endpoint at http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. `index.js` additionally exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions for any property access, so a consumer build importing named or default members of a legitimate internal `@cecm-web-sdk/core` resolves silently while the beacon reports the successful dependency-confusion resolution. The README self-labels the package as an authorized dependency-confusion test, but the beacon fires unconditionally on any machine that installs or requires the package, transmitting internal hostnames and filesystem paths in cleartext to a third-party bare-IP endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
